heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini prints Prusament PETG exceptionally well straight out of the box, reaching safe speeds up to 179 mm/s constrained by a 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. It requires no enclosure or hardened nozzle upgrades, though keeping the heated bed at its maximum 80°C is critical for proper adhesion.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with thin PVP glue stick or liquid release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 15 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent extrusion grinding during high-speed moves.
Limit maximum part cooling fan speed to 50% with layer time threshold between 30s and 12s to preserve layer adhesion.
Increase first layer bed temperature to 80°C and set nozzle temperature to 250°C for the initial layer, dropping to 248°C thereafter.
Enable 1.5mm retraction wipe and set Z-hop type to Spiral Z-hop to minimize nozzle stringing and blob deposition on perimeters.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine hair buildup
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Prusament PETG is highly hygroscopic and oozes readily when ambient moisture is absorbed, exacerbated by excessive nozzle temperature.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 65°C for 6 hours in a dedicated filament dryer and reduce nozzle printing temperature by 5°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PEI surface damage or violent over-adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically bonds directly to smooth and textured PEI coatings, risking coating tear-out upon part removal.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin layer of liquid glue or PVP glue stick as an interfacial release agent before starting the print.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Bed temperature dropping below the material's glass transition threshold due to room draft exposure on the open-frame A1 Mini.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lock bed temperature at 80°C, turn auxiliary cooling fans completely OFF, and apply a 5mm outer brim.

faq.question: Can the A1 Mini reach the recommended bed temperature for Prusament PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, Prusament recommends 75°C to 90°C. Setting the A1 Mini heated bed to its hardware limit of 80°C is sufficient for strong adhesion without thermal runaway.

faq.question: Do I need a hardened steel nozzle to print Prusament PETG on the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: No, standard Prusament PETG is non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 Mini handles it without premature wear.

faq.question: Why does Prusament PETG print slower than Bambu PETG Basic on the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: Prusament PETG possesses a higher molecular weight and melt viscosity, restricting safe volumetric flow to 15 mm³/s compared to high-flow variants.

faq.question: Can I leave Prusament PETG mounted on the A1 Mini spool holder between prints?
faq.answer: No, PETG absorbs ambient moisture within 24 to 48 hours, causing foaming, stringing, and brittle parts; store it in a sealed desiccant drybox when idle.
